newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN STOCK MARKET CLOSING REPORT.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN STOCK MARKET CLOSING REPORT.

text.p: South African shares dipped on Thursday as poor sentiment gripped the market, but sparkling results from Investec Bank Ltd triggered a surge of trade in the banking sector, dealers said.
The local market has been suffering the blues recently after a rash of poor corporate earnings in May crystalised concerns in the industrials sector.
The market also took a knock on Thursday from a dip on Wall Street on Wednesday and failed to respond to an early rise in New York shares on Thursday.
"It has been a quiet day, people are basically depressed about the short-term prospects for corporate earnings," one dealer said.

The all-share index dropped 31.1 points to 7,096.1 as the industrials index slipped 44.7 points to 8,351.5. Volumes were modest at 717 million rands worth of trade, but the figure was the highest of the week so far.
The main reason for the higher volumes was the interest sparked in the banking sector following the publication of Investec's year figures after the market closed on Wednesday.
Investec saw headline diluted earnings per share up 36.3 percent at 572.1 cents, well ahead of a Reuters poll of analysts who expected a rise to between 550.0 and 558.3 cents a share.
Investec jumped 6.00 rand to end at a new year high of 156.00 rand.

Elsewhere in the sector, Absa put on 15 cents to 30.00 rand in trade worth 66.1 million rand, Nedcor droped 25 cents to 89.75 rand in trade worth 47.1 million rand and Standard Bank was steady at 214.00 rand in deals worth 41.0 million rand.
Another large deal was a single institutional buy of about 3.7 million shares in Pick'n'Pay Holdings that saw the stock lose eight cents to 244 cents.

Big gainers were Momentum Life Assurers which gained almost nine percent to end at 566 cents and hotels firm Don Group Ltd which put on eight cents to 162 cents, after touching a high of 178 cents. Both stocks were recovering after prolonged selling.

However, shares in ailing chicken producer Rainbow Chicken Ltd slumped to a fresh year low of 77 cents as investors continued to bail out of the stock following heavy losses in the year to March. But the firm clawed back some ground to end down just one cent at 83 cents.

Gold shares had a weaker session after two days of gains as demand slackened and fresh concerns were raised about the price of bullion. Gold fixed a shade easier in London at $342.75 afer New York gold opened lower.
"Golds are starting to look a little overvalued," one dealer said.
The golds index lost 8.6 points to 1,205.5 as Western Deeps lost 50 cents to 120.50 rand, Kloof shed 10 cents to 30.25 rand and Vaal Reefs dipped 50 cents to 269.50 rand.
The futures market showed little sign of breaking the bad mood underlying South African shares at the moment, coming off early and staying at low levels all day in light trade.
The all-share June contract was last at 6,477/83 from 6,546 as the industrials contract slipped back to 8,128/35 from 8,202.
The golds contract was a touch firmer at 844/48 from 846.
